header: Too many requests for Search Backpressure
content:
CPU-based admission control is a gatekeeping mechanism that proactively limits the number of
requests to a node based on its current capacity, both for organic increases and spikes in traﬃc.
Excessive requests return an HTTP 429 “Too Many Requests” status code upon rejection. This errors
indicates either insuﬃcient cluster resources, resource-intensive search requests, or an unintended
spike in the workload.
Search Backpressure provides the reason for rejection, which can help ﬁne-tune resource-intensive
search requests. For traﬃc spikes, we recommend client-side retries with exponential backoﬀ and
jitter.
